title: Bear and Polynomials
statementMd:
Limak is a little polar bear. He doesn't have many toys and thus he often plays with polynomials.

He considers a polynomial *valid* if its degree is $*n*$ and its coefficients are integers not exceeding $*k*$ by the absolute value. More formally:

Let $*a*_{0}, *a*_{1}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ denote the coefficients, so ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/01a1124daa02c1ae8b4478acfb4184cd23b3d229.png). Then, a polynomial $*P*(*x*)$ is valid if all the following conditions are satisfied:

- $*a*_{*i*}$ is integer for every $*i*$;
- $|*a*_{*i*}| ≤ *k*$ for every $*i*$;
- $*a*_{*n*} ≠ 0$.

Limak has recently got a valid polynomial $*P*$ with coefficients $*a*_{0}, *a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$. He noticed that $*P*(2) ≠ 0$ and he wants to change it. He is going to change one coefficient to get a **valid** polynomial $*Q*$ of degree $*n*$ that $*Q*(2) = 0$. Count the number of ways to do so. You should count two ways as a distinct if coefficients of target polynoms differ.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $*n*$ and $*k*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 200 000, 1 ≤ *k* ≤ 10^{9}$) — the degree of the polynomial and the limit for absolute values of coefficients.

The second line contains $*n* + 1$ integers $*a*_{0}, *a*_{1}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ ($|*a*_{*i*}| ≤ *k*, *a*_{*n*} ≠ 0$) — describing a **valid** polynomial ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/01a1124daa02c1ae8b4478acfb4184cd23b3d229.png). It's guaranteed that $*P*(2) ≠ 0$.

## Output

Print the number of ways to change one coefficient to get a valid polynomial $*Q*$ that $*Q*(2) = 0$.

## Note

In the first sample, we are given a polynomial $*P*(*x*) = 10 - 9*x* - 3*x*^{2} + 5*x*^{3}$.

Limak can change one coefficient in three ways:

1. He can set $*a*_{0} = - 10$. Then he would get $*Q*(*x*) = - 10 - 9*x* - 3*x*^{2} + 5*x*^{3}$ and indeed $*Q*(2) = - 10 - 18 - 12 + 40 = 0$.
2. Or he can set $*a*_{2} = - 8$. Then $*Q*(*x*) = 10 - 9*x* - 8*x*^{2} + 5*x*^{3}$ and indeed $*Q*(2) = 10 - 18 - 32 + 40 = 0$.
3. Or he can set $*a*_{1} = - 19$. Then $*Q*(*x*) = 10 - 19*x* - 3*x*^{2} + 5*x*^{3}$ and indeed $*Q*(2) = 10 - 38 - 12 + 40 = 0$.

In the second sample, we are given the same polynomial. This time though, $*k*$ is equal to $12$ instead of $10^{9}$. Two first of ways listed above are still valid but in the third way we would get $|*a*_{1}| > *k*$ what is not allowed. Thus, the answer is $2$ this time.
statementZhMd:
Limak 是一只小北极熊。他没有很多玩具，因此经常和多项式一起玩。

如果一个多项式的次数为 $*n*$，且其系数均为整数并且绝对值不超过 $*k*$，那么他就称这个多项式是*有效的*。更正式地说：

设 $*a*_{0}, *a*_{1}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ 为多项式的系数，使得 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/01a1124daa02c1ae8b4478acfb4184cd23b3d229.png)。如果满足以下所有条件，则多项式 $*P*(*x*)$ 是有效的：

- 对于每个 $*i*$，$*a*_{*i*}$ 都是整数；
- 对于每个 $*i*$，$|*a*_{*i*}| ≤ *k*$；
- $*a*_{*n*} ≠ 0$。

Limak 最近得到了一个系数为 $*a*_{0}, *a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ 的有效多项式 $*P*$。他注意到 $*P*(2) ≠ 0$，因此想要对其进行修改。他将修改其中一个系数，得到一个次数为 $*n*$ 且满足 $*Q*(2) = 0$ 的**有效**多项式 $*Q*$。请计算修改的方法数。若最终得到的多项式系数不同，则视为不同的方法。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*k*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 200 000$，$1 ≤ *k* ≤ 10^{9}$）——多项式的次数和系数绝对值的上限。

第二行包含 $*n* + 1$ 个整数 $*a*_{0}, *a*_{1}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$（$|*a*_{*i*}| ≤ *k*$，$*a*_{*n*} ≠ 0$）——描述一个**有效**多项式 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/01a1124daa02c1ae8b4478acfb4184cd23b3d229.png)。保证 $*P*(2) ≠ 0$。

## 输出格式

输出修改一个系数后得到满足 $*Q*(2) = 0$ 的有效多项式 $*Q*$ 的方法数。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，给定的多项式为 $*P*(*x*) = 10 - 9*x* - 3*x*^{2} + 5*x*^{3}$。

Limak 有三种修改系数的方法：

1. 他可以令 $*a*_{0} = - 10$。这样得到的多项式为 $*Q*(*x*) = - 10 - 9*x* - 3*x*^{2} + 5*x*^{3}$，并且确实有 $*Q*(2) = - 10 - 18 - 12 + 40 = 0$。
2. 或者，他可以令 $*a*_{2} = - 8$。这样得到的多项式为 $*Q*(*x*) = 10 - 9*x* - 8*x*^{2} + 5*x*^{3}$，并且确实有 $*Q*(2) = 10 - 18 - 32 + 40 = 0$。
3. 或者，他可以令 $*a*_{1} = - 19$。这样得到的多项式为 $*Q*(*x*) = 10 - 19*x* - 3*x*^{2} + 5*x*^{3}$，并且确实有 $*Q*(2) = 10 - 38 - 12 + 40 = 0$。

在第二个样例中，给定的仍然是同一个多项式。但这次 $*k*$ 等于 $12$，而不是 $10^{9}$。上面列出的前两种方法仍然有效，但第三种方法会得到 $|*a*_{1}| > *k*$，这是不允许的。因此，这次答案为 $2$。
